title: Launch capacity safeguard and prioritization fabric for runtime/console/api rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As more runtime, console and API changes are staged for coordinated launches, there is no standard, machine-readable policy to prioritize slots and reserve surge capacity across Dedicated and Hosted tenants. That gap causes last-minute manual negotiations, contention during regional spikes, and inconsistent rollback behavior.

Objective: Build a reusable 'prioritization fabric' and capacity safeguard playbook that lets PMs and eng teams declare launch priority lanes, reserve hedged capacity, and attach automatic fallback/grade-of-service rules to rollout cohorts. The fabric should be policy-first (config declarative in the launch manifest), integrate with capacity signals (queues/metrics), and surface deterministic decisioning in the Console UI and the Launch Conductor API.

Scope (in):
- Define prioritization lanes (e.g., Critical, High, Standard, Background) and mapping rules to Dedicated pools, hosted fallback models, and regional quotas.
- Implement a capacity escrow prototype: ability to reserve tokenized capacity credits per launch slot for up to N hours prior to cutover.
- Add lightweight prioritization config schema to the Launch Conductor manifest (versioned).
- Console UX surface for launch owners to claim/preview reserved capacity and view preflight signals.
- Rollout policy hooks: automatic fallback to compatible model variants or reduced batch sizes when thresholds hit.

Scope (out):
- Full billing/commit accounting for reserved capacity (finance integration will be separate).
- Deep autoscaling algorithm changes to scheduler—fabric will call existing autoscaler signals.

Deliverables:
- PM spec + example manifests (Confluence).
- API contract for reserve/release capacity calls.
- Console preview and reservation UX flows (mockups + acceptance tests).
- Capacity escrow service prototype (limited to dedicated pools in us-west-2).
- Runbook for on-call and rollback triggers for launch owners.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Reduced last-minute slot reassignments by 60% for coordinated launches.
- ≥ 90% of launches using the fabric preflight signal pass automated capacity checks.
- Mean time to cutover issues related to capacity decreases by 25%.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Manifest schema v1 merged in Launch Conductor repo and documented. 2) Reserve/release API endpoints implemented and smoke-tested against a dedicated pool. 3) Console shows reservation preview, owner can claim/release, and audit log entries are created. 4) Runbook and rollback playbook reviewed and signed off by SRE and Runtime leads. 5) Demo with three cross-functional teams (runtime, console, API) executed reporting metrics in dashboard.

comments: 2025-01-13 — Asha: Initial draft spec posted to Confluence; scheduled cross-functional review for 2025-01-16.

2025-01-16 — Diego (Runtime): We prefer non-blocking escrow semantics; prototype should use soft reservations with TTL and penalty signals instead of hard capacity carve-outs. Follow-up: define penalty matrix.
2025-01-18 — Priya (SRE): Need clarity on who can claim/release on-call; proposed policy: only launch owner + SRE runbook approval for >2x baseline reservations.
2025-01-21 — UX review (Marta): Mockups look ok; request: show estimated cost delta and fallback plan in the preview modal. Action: add 'estimated cost' line in mock by 2025-01-24.

2025-01-28 — Luca: Decided on two-tier prototype: (1) soft escrow (default) and (2) optional hard escrow for enterprise customers (requires billing flow). Logged PM-451900 to cover billing integration.
2025-02-03 — Engineering sync: API signatures agreed (reserve/release/status). ENG-8712 assigned to implement API stubs; expected PR by 2025-02-10.

2025-02-06 — Preflight smoke: staging deploy passed basic reservation and release cycle; observed contention window when multiple owners reserve overlapping regional slots; mitigation: add per-region tie-breaker rule and update manifest docs.
2025-02-08 — Asha: Updated acceptance criteria to include audit log verification and demo schedule. Added pilot target team: Marketing Search.
communications_plan: - Preflight announcement in #launch-orchestration 1 week before pilot. - Pilot owner playbook shared via Confluence and announced to GTM/SEs. - Post-pilot readout + decision: expand to other teams or iterate (2-week window).
risk_register: - Risk: Over-reservation causing underutilization during normal hours. Mitigation: soft escrow TTL and automatic release triggers; monitoring dashboard to surface unused reservations after 30 minutes. - Risk: Confusion about priority lanes across regions. Mitigation: canonical mapping table in Confluence and Console tooltip. - Risk: Enterprise customers expect guaranteed capacity (billing). Mitigation: flag enterprise launches and route to hard-escrow beta only with finance sign-off.
notes_for_engineering: - Start with idempotent reserve/release APIs with request-id for at-least-once semantics. - TTL-based soft reservations with a 'renew' call. - Expose reservation state via Launch Conductor status endpoints for Console to poll. - Integrate with existing autoscaler signals; do not change core scheduler in prototype. - Add audit events to the event bus for all reserve/release actions.
next_steps: 1) ENG: API stub (ENG-8712) by 2025-02-10. 2) UX: update mock with cost estimate line by 2025-01-24 (Marta). 3) Runbook: draft rollback criteria and publish by 2025-02-12 (Priya). 4) Schedule pilot with Marketing Search for week of 2025-03-03.
